title: Reimagining On-Shelf Availability with Agentic AI
gist: BCG argues retailers have largely solved out-of-stock detection yet still see 5%-15% out-of-stock rates because diagnosis and ownership are fragmented across forecasting, suppliers, distribution and stores. Its agentic AI platform AVA coordinates specialized agents to move from signal to root cause to accountable action, letting one US retailer proactively address 70% of identified availability issues within a quarter; BCG recommends starting with high-value failure modes rather than a wholesale overhaul.

insights.claim: Despite a decade of investment in point-of-sale alerts, gap scans, inventory dashboards, computer vision and analytics, BCG observes retail out-of-stock rates of 5% to 15% depending on product category, representing significant lost sales.
insights.speaker: Yasemin Gunay
insights.so_what: Availability remains a large unrecovered revenue pool for grocers and mass retailers; vendors that only add more detection tooling face diminishing returns.
insights.quote: we have seen out-of-stock rates reach 5% to 15%, depending on the product category
insights.locator: Retail has gotten better at filling

insights.claim: Retail availability tools reveal what is out of stock, where and when, but not why; a single out-of-stock can stem from a forecasting miss, buyer under-ordering, supplier shorting, late distribution-center arrival or store ordering error, each tied to a different data source, system and owner.
insights.speaker: Yasemin Gunay
insights.so_what: The value in retail analytics is shifting from detection to root-cause diagnosis across fragmented systems; watch for vendors positioned on cross-system reasoning.
insights.quote: Yet the deeper insight into the root cause, that is, the “why,” remains elusive.
insights.locator: Retailers Know What and Where; the Harder Question Is Why

insights.claim: When the root cause of a retail out-of-stock is unclear, the issue rolls downhill to stores as alerts, tasks and exception lists, so store teams treat symptoms even when the real cause sits upstream in forecasting, suppliers or distribution.
insights.speaker: Yasemin Gunay
insights.so_what: Store labor productivity is being consumed by upstream failures; retailers fixing upstream diagnosis could release store labor cost, not just recover sales.
insights.quote: When the root cause is unclear, the issue rolls downhill to the store in the form of alerts, tasks, and exception lists.
insights.locator: This fragmentation creates a structural problem

insights.claim: BCG argues product availability should be treated as an end-to-end supply-chain system outcome rather than a store metric alone.
insights.speaker: Yasemin Gunay
insights.so_what: Retail KPIs and incentives anchored on store-level availability misassign accountability; operating-model redesign is the lever.
insights.quote: Availability, therefore, should not be treated as a store metric alone. It is an end-to-end system outcome.
insights.locator: This fragmentation creates a structural problem

insights.claim: Availability gaps persist between retailers and CPG manufacturers despite years of data sharing and better forecasting because accountability is split across buyers, replenishment planners, CPG sales analysts, supplier customer-service, distribution and store teams, with no single player owning the end-to-end outcome.
insights.speaker: Yasemin Gunay
insights.so_what: More data-sharing deals between retailers and CPG firms will not by themselves fix out-of-stocks; look for clear end-to-end ownership models.
insights.quote: no single player owns the end-to-end outcome
insights.locator: Availability Is an Ownership Problem as Much as a Data Problem

insights.claim: BCG contends that more data does not solve retail out-of-stocks; historically the problem was hard to fix at scale because no person, function or system was chartered to reason continuously across the whole availability chain, a constraint agentic AI removes.
insights.speaker: Yasemin Gunay
insights.so_what: Positions agentic AI as an organizational unlock rather than a data/analytics upgrade, a different buying rationale for retail AI spend.
insights.quote: More data does not solve that problem.
insights.locator: One reason is that accountability is distributed

insights.claim: An agentic availability system differs from an alerting system by analyzing point-of-sale, inventory, forecast, vendor, logistics, planogram, promotion and store-execution data collectively rather than sequentially, then outputting the problem, likely cause, value at stake, required action and accountable owner.
insights.speaker: Yasemin Gunay
insights.so_what: Defines the product spec that separates agentic retail AI from legacy dashboards; useful for evaluating retail-tech vendors' claims.
insights.quote: “Here is the problem, here is the likely cause, here is the value at stake, here is the action required, and here is who should take that action.”
insights.locator: Agents Can Close the Loop from Signal to Action

insights.claim: BCG argues disconnected AI pilots deliver limited availability benefits; real gains require an architecture in which specialized agents connect into workflows, governance and decision rights.
insights.speaker: Yasemin Gunay
insights.so_what: Retail AI value accrues to integrated orchestration layers over point solutions, favoring platform-style vendors and consultancies selling end-to-end programs.
insights.quote: Building a collection of disconnected AI pilots can only ever offer limited benefits.
insights.locator: AVA: From Individual Agents to an Integrated Availability Platform

insights.claim: BCG's AVA is a modular suite of agents acting as a coordinating layer that identifies availability opportunities, quantifies impact, diagnoses root causes, routes actions into workflows and learns from each outcome for future planning.
insights.speaker: Yasemin Gunay
insights.so_what: BCG is productizing agentic AI in retail operations, a sign consultancies are moving into software-like offerings competing with retail-tech vendors.
insights.locator: BCG’s AVA is a modular suite of agents

insights.claim: AVA divides work across specialized agents: a supplier and DC readiness agent monitors vendor inbound and distribution-center inventory to route recovery before stores are hit; a store inventory and shelf execution agent finds product in-store but not on shelf and prioritizes by sales exposure; a root cause and learning agent quantifies outcomes and feeds recurring causes back into planning.
insights.speaker: Yasemin Gunay
insights.so_what: Shows a reusable multi-agent decomposition of the retail supply chain that other operators can copy.
insights.locator: AVA allows different agents to address different parts

insights.claim: A leading US retailer that previously detected availability issues only after sales were lost, with limited supplier/inbound visibility and product stuck in receiving or the backroom, proactively addressed 70% of identified availability issues within one quarter after deploying BCG's AVA agents.
insights.speaker: Yasemin Gunay
insights.so_what: A vendor-reported (not independently verified) result suggesting agentic availability tools can show impact within a quarter; watch for retailers citing similar out-of-stock gains in earnings.
insights.quote: Within one quarter, the retailer was able to proactively address 70% of identified availability issues.
insights.locator: The model has already produced results for a leading US retailer

insights.claim: BCG advises retailers not to wait for a perfect data environment or launch a massive transformation, but to start process by process: pick the highest-value availability failure modes, define required decisions, clarify ownership and deploy agents where cross-system reasoning materially improves outcomes.
insights.speaker: Yasemin Gunay
insights.so_what: Implies retail agentic AI adoption will be incremental and use-case led, favoring modular tools over large ERP-style overhauls.
insights.quote: Getting there does not require waiting for a perfect data environment or launching a massive transformation.
insights.locator: Getting there does not require waiting

insights.claim: The goal of agentic availability is not to automate every decision but to have machines handle continuous detection, synthesis and root-cause reasoning while people focus on exceptions requiring human judgment.
insights.speaker: Yasemin Gunay
insights.so_what: Signals human-in-the-loop augmentation rather than headcount elimination as the near-term retail AI model.
insights.quote: The goal should not be to automate every single availability decision.
insights.locator: The goal should not be to automate
